definitions.explanation: A written or electronic reply to a message, email, or letter. The act of sending such a reply.

examples.japanese: メールに{返信|へんしん}する。
{返信|へんしん}が{遅|おそ}くなってすみません。
メッセージを{送|おく}ったのに{一週間|いっしゅうかん}たっても{返信|へんしん}が{来|こ}なくて{心配|しんぱい}している。
examples.english: I sent a message but haven't received a reply even after a week, so I'm worried.

notes:
Compound of {返|へん} (return) + {信|しん} (message, letter). Used as a suru-verb: {返信|へんしん}する (to reply).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {返信|へんしん}する (to reply)
- {返信|へんしん}が{来|く}る (a reply arrives)
- {返信|へんしん}が{遅|おそ}い (a reply is late)
- {返信|へんしん}をもらう (to receive a reply)
- ご{返信|へんしん} (polite: your reply)

USAGE NOTE:
Not to be confused with the homophone {変身|へんしん} (transformation). {返信|へんしん} specifically refers to replying to correspondence. For replying in general conversation, {返事|へんじ} is more common. {返答|へんとう} is more formal and used for answering questions directly.
